legitimate_experiment_differences: Fixed32 uses extra exponent offset5 in every lower-precision block; Fixed64 uses offset6.
Learned100 adds4080 FP32 theta parameters and their explicit surrogate gradient; hard lower offsets choose5/6 per block.
Freeze50 shares learned epochs1–50 exactly and then retains the epoch50 theta/choices; it restores actual checkpoint55 for56–100.
Freeze50 still computes theta gradients and Adam moments with theta LR0; it is not an optimized-cost implementation.
conclusion: Existing files suffice for the four-way accuracy/curve/checkpoint comparison without training or checkpoint reevaluation. Fixed64 exceeds Freeze50 in all three epoch100 accuracies; Fixed32 exceeds Freeze50 in both lower precisions but is lower in E4M3.
limitations: Exactly one shared seed, no independent repeated-seed estimate; nondeterministic CUDA backend remains enabled.
Checkpoint selection uses the official test set, so selected maxima are not independent validation estimates.
Global E4-best of learned100 and freeze50 is the same shared pre-freeze epoch34 and must be labelled as such.
Matched51–100 selection is additional, and all three modes must come from its one E4-selected epoch per method.
The fixed32 archive contains all600 train/test metric rows and full report, but no raw history. No independent per-epoch order-hash verification is claimed for fixed32.
Dataset and checkpoint identities are checked from recorded metadata; no binary checkpoint or SVHN data is loaded here.

Session times mix different laptop sessions and diagnostic implementations. They do not establish hardware speedup; freeze continuation time must not be compared to a complete100-epoch run as if it covered all100.
